_meta.admission_rule: No entry is marked published without at least one measurement carrying a value AND a source file. Prose alone does not qualify.

measurements.metric: negative-test catch rate — distribution gate, tolerance/ratio policy
measurements.how_measured: 1,000 injected plausible pp/% values (seeded uniform 0.6–80.0) across the 25 nearest-to-flip signals, each scoped to that signal's own declared ground truth; measured the share the gate rejected under two policies — core.traceability.SIBC with ratio grounding vs the new DISTRIBUTION policy without it.

measurements.metric: false-rejection rate on true statements — same gate
measurements.how_measured: Ran the real, uncorrupted watchlist sentence for the 25 nearest-to-flip signals through the same check. The 3 failures were the glued-'pp' extractor backtrack (1.9pp -> 1), fixed by the spaced format; locked by test_real_watchlist_sentences_are_never_falsely_rejected.

measurements.metric: newsletter gate (validate_newsletter.check_doc) catch rate — BEFORE rescoping
measurements.how_measured: analysis/measure_groundedness.py, 200 injections per attack across the 3 live issues (release read x2 + deep read), seed 7. Verified by hand: the gate passed 9.1%, 47.3% and 812.6% injected into a body paragraph, and only rejected a 5-figure absurdity.

measurements.metric: newsletter gate catch rate — AFTER per-block scoping + DISTRIBUTION policy
measurements.how_measured: Same harness, same seed, same issues. Three changes: per-block scope with NO issue-wide fallback; core.traceability.DISTRIBUTION policy (rounding width, no ratio grounding); ground truth includes each value as fmt_value renders it. Rendered .md output byte-identical before and after.

measurements.metric: scope width — values a single paragraph was checked against
measurements.value: 735 (289 distinct) → 0 for undeclared blocks, ~10-35 for declared ones
measurements.how_measured: declared_ground_truth() on a release read's 21 declared signals, before vs after per-block scoping.

measurements.metric: distribution gate catch rate — same harness, for comparison
measurements.how_measured: analysis/measure_groundedness.py --gate distribution. Weaker than the newsletter because a claim's scope includes its full period series and ranges, which prose legitimately references ('16-period range'). Next tightening target.

measurements.metric: newsletter gate catch rate by decision point — D1 (per-block scope, the real test)
measurements.how_measured: measure_groundedness.py rewritten to inject at EVERY eligible block (was: first p block only). 50 injections per attack per site over 44 D1 blocks across the 3 long-form issues; each block scoped to exactly the signals it declares. near-miss = a real value nudged past rounding; in-range = a fresh value from the doc's own range, caught only by scope.

measurements.metric: newsletter gate in-range catch rate by scope band — the scope-width/leak relationship, measured
measurements.how_measured: same run, D1 blocks bucketed by distinct candidate-value count. in-range fabrications (the scope-only attack) are caught ~100% at narrow scope and fall to ~79% once a block's ground truth runs to hundreds/thousands of values — the deep read's basis lines (scope up to 2306) are the wide band. near-miss stays high (tolerance catches it) regardless of width. This is the leading indicator the old harness could not see.

measurements.metric: distribution gate catch rate by decision point — D3 per-claim + D4 blurb (current data)
measurements.value: D3 100.0%/100.0%, D4 100.0%/100.0% (0 false rejections); only 1 generated claim exists this vintage (other slots all-verbatim)
measurements.how_measured: same harness, check_slate. Today only the 28th (C8 watchlist) emits a non-verbatim claim; 1st/7th/14th are all verbatim feed cards (number-checked upstream at D5), so the slot number-injection surface is legitimately thin — scope width 67, both bands narrow, everything caught.

measurements.value: template-reject 100.0% (4/4 static share signals below the read floor); catch 54.5% (12/22 magnitude outliers scored >= floor 2.0)
measurements.how_measured: analysis/signals/is_news.py --measure. Selector scores each L1 signal 2*record + 2*regime-flip + 1*crossed; a read must clear floor 2.0 (a strong factor). Ground truth is INDEPENDENT of the score: templates = share-method signals that also barely moved (<0.5x typical monthly move) -> must score below floor; news = magnitude outliers (>2x typical move) -> should clear floor. Magnitude is deliberately NOT a selector factor, so catch<100% is by design (a big move inside an established trend that sets no record and flips no regime is not a 'read').

measurements.metric: merged monthly issue — number gate catch by decision point (D1 per-block)
measurements.how_measured: analysis/measure_groundedness.py --gate newsletter, over the two live long-form cases (merged monthly_issue + deep_read), injecting at EVERY eligible block. D1 = blocks that declare signals; each scoped to exactly those signals.

measurements.metric: merged monthly issue — number gate catch by scope band (the width/leak curve)
measurements.how_measured: same run, D1 blocks bucketed by distinct candidate-value count. Same relationship the harness fix first exposed: narrow scope catches ~everything, wide scope leaks ~1-in-5 in-range fabrications. The monthly issue's own blocks are narrow (tiles 1-2 signals, flip lines 1 signal); the 1k+ band is the deep read's evidence_all basis lines (step-3 D1 fix target).

measurements.metric: merged monthly issue — word-vs-number agreement check (NEW, first non-number-tracing check since 2g)
measurements.value: catch 100.0% (11/11 injected direction/rate contradictions), 0 false positives on the clean issue
measurements.how_measured: negate the rate sign on each generated flip line (the real 'status says up, YoY is -2.6%' class); validate_distribution.word_number_conflicts must hard-fail each. Clean doc must produce 0 conflicts. The check reads only %/pp rates (a level like Rs 2.95L Cr has no direction) and fires when a line's single direction cue disagrees with its rate; conflicts in verbatim card prose warn instead of fail (fixed upstream at v1.12).

measurements.metric: merged monthly issue (§11.1 REVISED, with sector/bank tables) — number gate catch by decision point
measurements.value: D1 per-block near-miss 99.6%, in-range 96.0% (0/68 false rejections); bands 1-50→99.9%, 201-1k→93.1%, 1k+→85.0% in-range
measurements.how_measured: analysis/measure_groundedness.py --gate newsletter after the §11.1 revision (flip-list→sector growth table, banks→3 tables, fleet→prose). Harness extended to inject into the NEW `table` block type (per-row, scoped to the row's own signal) — without that the table numbers, most of the issue's figures, went unattacked (D1 sites 24→68). Supersedes the pre-revision merged-issue entry. The narrow table rows (1 signal each) catch ~100%; the 1k+ band that leaks ~15% in-range is the deep read's evidence_all basis lines (step-3 D1 fix target), not the monthly issue.

observations: The +9.99 pp incident (2026-07-21): an invented pair-divergence value PASSED the first negative test because the signal was classified scan-like, pooling a pp gap with two pct rates and deriving cumulative sums. Fixing the classification made the same corruption hard-fail. Lesson: a groundedness check is only as good as the ground-truth shape it compares against.
First newsletter traceability cut was vacuous — period-wide scope let invented numbers pass. Rescoping to declared signals only was the fix. Same lesson as Check 4f's evidence_all rescoping.
Negative testing must target the artifact the validator actually reads. The pair-divergence negative test only worked after editing analysis/rbi_atm_pos/insights.json rather than the web copy.

Loosening a gate can be invisible: the distribution gate initially inherited the card policy (abs_tol=0.25 plus ratio grounding) and passed every negative test I threw at it — not because the text was grounded but because a 29-value pool spawns ~800 candidate ratios and a quarter-point tolerance covers most of the number line worth inventing. Catch rate 41.5%. The same check, scoped to rounding width and with ratio grounding removed, catches 95.7%. A gate that never fails is not evidence of correctness; measure the catch rate.

Groundedness has two error rates, and only measuring one is how you ship a gate that blocks the truth. Tightening tolerance took false rejections from 0 to 3/25 until the formatting quirk behind them was fixed; both numbers belong in the measurement.

The gate guarding the subscriber-facing newsletter caught 0% of invented numbers, and had passed every hand-written negative test since it was built. Hand-written negative tests select for numbers the author already suspects; an injection harness does not. Every gate needs a measured catch rate before it can be described as working.

A defensive default is a hole. When per-block scoping was added, blocks with no declared signals fell back to the issue-wide pool 'so nothing breaks' — that single fallback dropped the in-range catch rate from 91.9% to 42.4%, because the injection site was exactly such a block. Removing the fallback took it to 99.5%. Scope defaults should fail closed.

Tightening surfaced two real bugs that the loose gate had been hiding, both display-format rather than data problems: values rendered for the reader (₹2.9L Cr, 12.0 crore) did not match their stored form, and ratio grounding had been silently accepting them as a/b of other values. The fix — ground the value through the same renderer the issue uses — is exact rather than a tolerance guess.

CORRECTION to the 2026-07-21 newsletter entries (100.0%/99.5% near-miss/in-range): those numbers measured decision point D2, not the gate. The old measure_groundedness.py:138 injected into the FIRST p block then broke; in the deep read that block is the signal-less intro, which grounds nothing and fails closed. All 200 injections hit one always-fail block. The blocks that can actually leak — basis lines scoped to thousands of values — were never attacked. This is the FOURTH appearance of the narrow-negative-test failure class (Check 4f period-wide -> newsletter v1 -> distribution -> the harness itself). Fixed 2026-07-23: inject every eligible block, report per decision point and per scope band, never one pooled number.

The honest newsletter picture after the fix: D1 in-range catch is 92.8% pooled but that pooling hides the real story — it is 100% up to ~200 candidate values and 79% beyond 1000. Scope width, not tolerance, is what a wide-scope gate leaks on. This is the empirical case for the deep-read D1 scope fix (basis lines -> member's own signal instead of the driver's whole evidence_all set): narrowing scope is expected to move those wide-band blocks from 79% back toward 100%.

Method lesson banked for the track: automating a negative test freezes the author's choice of injection SITE, not just their choice of value. A catch rate is only trustworthy sliced by the scope of the site attacked; a single artifact-level number is the same vacuity as a single period-wide ground-truth pool, one level up.

is-news selector design: the first cut flipped on ~50% of signals because status wobbles accelerating<->decelerating (strengthening<->active) every noisy month while still growing. Fixed by counting a flip only on a REGIME change (growing<->shrinking<->flat), not the within-regime wobble; the wobble is demoted to the weakest factor (crossed, weight 1) and can never make something a read alone. Second finding: labelling ALL share signals as templates was too coarse -- a share at an all-time reversal record (credit-cards' share of personal loans) is a legitimate read, not a template. The clean template is a share that ALSO didn't move.

Building the merged monthly issue surfaced 6 advice/forecast warnings in verbatim card prose (the is-news reads inherit LLM-eval consulting-speak: 'Lenders should allocate capital exclusively to UPI QR', 'the ratio will continue widening through FY27'). These are WARNINGS not failures by design (Sec 11.1 / Sec 5.3): card prose is the eval's, fixed upstream at prompt v1.12, never hand-edited in the renderer. The new prose_lint's advice+forecast detectors make that fix list visible for the first time -- 6 concrete card-prose items feeding v1.12.

is-news + magnitude factor (reco b): adding magnitude (>2x typical move, weight 2) surfaced large-corporate +14.4% YoY as a credit read it would have missed on record/regime alone. Trade-off measured: selectivity rose to 48.7% of signals clearing the read floor this cycle (a broad-growth month) -- the top-2 reads stay unambiguous but 'a read is the exception' weakens; tunable via MAGNITUDE_MULT. Template-reject held at 100%. Second note: the word-vs-number check had a false-positive class on legitimate 'fell 4.3%' prose (word carries the sign, magnitude is unsigned); fixed by firing only on EXPLICITLY-signed rates (the real 'up, -2.6%' bug), plus word-boundary cues so bare up/down fire without tripping on group/update.
open_questions: Breadth-based (period-wide) checks let an in-range invented number pass. What is the cheapest scoping that closes this for free prose, not just structured values?
Can groundedness be measured as a single rate across both pipelines, or is it inherently per-check?
